content:
The image shows soybean plants with the following observations:

- Mostly green foliage, but with some yellowing leaves scattered throughout, particularly in the lower/inner canopy
- Some leaves appear wilted or collapsed (visible yellow/tan collapsed leaves at the base)
- The yellowing pattern appears systemic rather than localized spots
- No clear fungal pustules, spots, or lesions visible on individual leaves
- The plant appears to have some general chlorosis/yellowing and collapse of lower leaves
- Stems appear to remain somewhat green while leaves yellow

This pattern — yellowing of lower leaves, premature leaf drop/collapse, with green stems remaining — is characteristic of **Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS)**. SDS causes interveinal chlorosis and necrosis of leaves while the stem interior turns brown, but externally the stem can appear green. The scattered yellowing and wilting pattern across the canopy is consistent with this.

Alternative: Green_stem_disorder also involves green stems with yellowing/dying leaves, but SDS fits better given the wilting and collapse pattern visible.
